title: The Life of Pythagoras, with Hierocles on the Golden Verses
author: Dacier and Rowe (trans)
description: The Life of Pythagoras, with his Symbols and Golden Verses, together with the Life of Hierocles and his Commentaries upon the Verses, translated from the French of André Dacier (first published in English in 1707, the version here attributed in the index to Dacier and Nicholas Rowe). Dacier's life of Pythagoras gathers ancient testimonies on the Samian sage's travels to Egypt and the East, his community at Croton, his teaching on number, harmony, the transmigration of souls, purification and silence, and the death of the master. The Golden Verses are the short Pythagorean poem of moral and spiritual precepts. The commentary of Hierocles of Alexandria, a fifth-century Neoplatonist, interprets them as a complete course of philosophical life, from civic virtue through purification to deification. It is an important early modern vehicle for the Pythagorean revival in English esotericism.
editionNote: Curator-supplied PDF and EPUB from the organised ebook collection. One format was converted from the other (EPUB from PDF). Source text obtained from the Internet Archive (https://archive.org/details/lifepythagorasw00hiergoog).
